steps.description:
It's time to introduce logic to your codes. In this unit, we will learn how to use the Button sensor to interact with your program with Conditional loop. Let's start with understanding the Button sensor.
The "Display Text" option on the LCD block allows you to enter a text. It also allows you to attach a sensor block so that you can see the value sent out by the sensor. To do that, you need to use the Create-text-with block to convert the sensor value to a text for the LCD to display. 

The Button sensor block continually sends a value to the robot.


Repeatedly show the Button sensor value on the LCD.

Take note of the displayed values, as they’ll be used later to define logical conditions.

  • Check the value displayed when the Button is not pressed.
  • Check the value displayed when the Button is pressed.
  • Check the value displayed when the Button is pressed twice.

Adjust the duration of the LCD block to see how it affects the response speed.

Repeat While and Repeat Until are two conditional loops with the opposite meaning. This is how they work:



Below is an example of a condition. The condition is True if Button D22 is pressed (the value it returns is equal to 1)


You can make use of the following Wait-Until block, too. It will do nothing and wait until the indicated button is pressed or released.



Make your robot perform the following sequence:

  1. Display "Press D22 to end" until the Button D22 is pressed.
  2. Then clear screen and end the program.

Use Repeat Until, Repeat While or Wait Until blocks in your code.

Many restaurants now rely on self-ordering through apps and kiosks, making the process faster and more convenient. Having learnt conditional loops and button sensor, this challenge will let you apply your knowledge to create a self-ordering kiosk.
